edges.effect_quant: Systematic reviews drawing on randomized studies suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: These interventions target Depression remission through very different pathways: antidepressants alter monoaminergic and downstream neuroplastic signaling, while CBT changes appraisal, avoidance, and learned behavioral loops. That is why effect size can vary with symptom subtype, adherence, and baseline severity.
edges.summary: Systematic reviews drawing on randomized studies link antidepressant treatment to favorable shifts in depression remission in adults with major depressive disorder. The average effect is usually moderate rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
